facts.text: Lake Shore was first settled in the 17th century as part of Maryland’s earliest colonial county, evolving into a suburban community by the 20th century.
Despite its name, Lake Shore sits inland from Chesapeake Bay; the bay’s influence still shapes its climate and seafood culture.
Lake Shore lies on the Hog Neck peninsula, bordered by tidal inlets like Magothy River to the south and Main Creek to the northeast.
Maryland Route 177, known locally as Mountain Road, cuts east–west through the center of the peninsula and has been the main thoroughfare since the community’s early days.
The area hosts several marinas and parks that offer boating and fishing opportunities, reflecting its long‑standing connection to the bay’s waters.
